title: GAIL Profit More Than Doubles as Gas Marketing Revenue Jumps 31%
excerpt: GAIL reported standalone profit of Rs 4,650 crore for the September quarter and gave in-principle approval to list GAIL Gas through an IPO diluting up to 25%.
body:
• GAIL (India) standalone net profit rose to Rs 4,650 crore in the September quarter, from Rs 2,217 crore a year earlier, as gas marketing revenue jumped more than 31%.
  • Consolidated net profit was about Rs 4,724 crore, with total income of about Rs 47,474 crore in Q2 FY27.
  • The board gave in-principle approval to list GAIL Gas through an IPO diluting up to 25%, with a launch expected in FY28.
  • For investors, transmission volume rose to 130.10 mscmd and marketing volume to 97.23 mscmd, while first-half capex reached Rs 7,600 crore against a planned Rs 12,900 crore for the year.

State-owned GAIL (India) posted a more than twofold rise in quarterly profit on Friday, helped by strong growth in its natural gas marketing business, according to Reuters. The company, described by Reuters as India's top natural gas distributor by market share, said net profit after tax rose to 46.5 billion rupees, or $489.3 million, for the quarter ended September 30, from 22.17 billion rupees a year ago.

On a consolidated basis, GAIL reported net profit of around Rs 4,724 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 1,989 crore a year earlier and Rs 4,671 crore in the first quarter, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Consolidated total income rose to around Rs 47,474 crore, from Rs 35,894 crore in the same quarter last year.

Gas marketing drives the quarter

The gas marketing segment was the largest contributor. Reuters reported that segment revenue rose more than 31% to 412.26 billion rupees. Revenue from petrochemicals rose nearly 26%, and revenue from natural gas transmission rose 21%. Total revenue from operations rose more than 30% to 459.24 billion rupees on a standalone basis, while expenses climbed more than 23%.

BusinessLine gave the operating volumes behind those numbers. Natural gas transmission volume stood at 130.10 million standard cubic meters per day, compared with 122.36 mscmd a year ago. Gas marketing volume rose to 97.23 mscmd from 93.82 mscmd, and LPG transmission volume stood at 1,130 thousand tonnes against 1,077 thousand tonnes a year earlier.

"Throughout this challenging period, our teams have demonstrated remarkable resilience and agility, ensuring that operations continue seamlessly despite the prevailing headwinds."

— Deepak Gupta, Chairman and Managing Director, GAIL (India)

Supply disruption in the background

The results came despite a supply disruption that GAIL disclosed in its filing. BusinessLine reported that, from March 2026, LNG supplies from the Middle East have been disrupted due to the geopolitical situation in West Asia, and that Petronet LNG declared force majeure on March 3, 2026, reducing RLNG allocation under the contract to zero from March 4. GAIL said it took mitigation measures, including procurement of LNG and natural gas from the spot market and alternative sources.

Reuters put that disruption in a wider demand context. India's gas consumption recovered to pre-Middle East conflict levels in September, Jefferies analysts had said ahead of earnings, and GAIL Chairman Deepak Gupta had said in September that supplies had resumed to almost 90% to 95% as the company ramped up its capability to buy LNG from elsewhere.

GAIL Gas listing approved in principle

Alongside the results, the board approved a separate corporate move. GAIL said in a BSE filing quoted by BusinessLine that the board "accorded in-principle approval for listing of shares of GAIL Gas, (a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL) (GGL) on the Indian stock exchanges through IPO route by diluting GAIL's equity in GGL up to 25 per cent."

Reuters reported the same approval, noting it is subject to final board approval. BusinessLine added that after GAIL Gas submits a final proposal based on recommendations from book running lead managers on valuation, price band, modality and other terms, the GAIL board will approve the final extent of dilution and terms. The IPO is expected to be launched in FY28. GAIL Gas is implementing city gas distribution projects in 16 geographical areas, with joint-venture activity in Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Vadodara, Haridwar, North Goa and Assam, according to BusinessLine.

What to watch

For the first half of FY27, GAIL recorded cumulative capital expenditure of Rs 7,600 crore, including Rs 1,425 crore in the second quarter, against planned annual capex of around Rs 12,900 crore, BusinessLine reported. Investors will watch whether marketing volumes hold at the higher level, whether alternative LNG sourcing keeps supply steady, and how the GAIL Gas proposal takes shape ahead of a final board decision.
